title: The Central Limit Theorem in 90 seconds

sentences.text: Roll one die, and every number from one to six is equally likely. The picture is flat.
sentences.tts: Roll one die, and every number from one to six is equally likely. The picture is flat.

sentences.text: Now roll ten dice, average them, and repeat that thousands of times.
sentences.tts: Now roll ten dice, average them, and repeat that thousands of times.

sentences.text: The averages pile up into a bell.
sentences.tts: The averages pile up into a bell.

sentences.text: This is the Central Limit Theorem.
sentences.tts: This is the Central Limit Theorem.

sentences.text: Take many independent samples from almost any population with finite variance, and the sample means become approximately normal.
sentences.tts: Take many independent samples from almost any population with finite variance, and the sample means become approximately normal.

sentences.text: They centre on the true mean, μ, and their spread, the standard error, is σ divided by the square root of n.
sentences.tts: They center on the true mean, mu, and their spread, the standard error, is sigma, divided by the square root of n.

sentences.text: Why does this happen? In an average, high and low values cancel each other out.
sentences.tts: Why does this happen? In an average, high and low values cancel each other out.

sentences.text: And there are far more combinations that land near the middle than at the edges.
sentences.tts: And there are far more combinations that land near the middle than at the edges.

sentences.text: Even strongly skewed data, like waiting times, are smoothed into a bell once the samples are large enough.
sentences.tts: Even strongly skewed data, like waiting times, are smoothed into a bell once the samples are large enough.

sentences.text: The idea took two centuries to build.
sentences.tts: The idea took two centuries to build.

sentences.text: Abraham de Moivre found the bell in coin tosses in 1733. Laplace generalised it around 1810, Lyapunov proved it in 1901, and George Pólya named it in 1920.
sentences.tts: Abraham de Moivre found the bell in coin tosses in seventeen thirty-three. Laplace generalized it around eighteen ten, Lyapunov proved it in nineteen oh one, and George Polya named it in nineteen twenty.

sentences.text: Today it sits underneath confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, opinion polls, clinical trials, A/B tests, and the control charts that keep factories on target.
sentences.tts: Today it sits underneath confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, opinion polls, clinical trials, A B tests, and the control charts that keep factories on target.

sentences.text: Whenever research reports an average with a margin of error, this theorem is quietly doing the work.
sentences.tts: Whenever research reports an average with a margin of error, this theorem is quietly doing the work.

sentences.text: Just remember the conditions: independent observations, finite variance, and bigger samples for skewed data.
sentences.tts: Just remember the conditions: independent observations, finite variance, and bigger samples for skewed data.

sentences.text: Now open the lab, and watch the bell appear for yourself.
sentences.tts: Now open the lab, and watch the bell appear for yourself.
